reference.name: Lijiang
reference.note: The itinerary uses Lijiang as the overnight base city (returning to Lijiang by bus); the afternoon walk is in its old town (Dayan).

variants.name: ok
variants.rationale: Name, region and country are right for Lijiang city, but locality 'Lhasa' is a different city in Tibet, hundreds of km away. (A and B agree.)

variants.name: ok
variants.rationale: Lijiang city, Yunnan, China: matches the base city the itinerary means. (A and B agree.)

variants.name: ok
variants.rationale: Card narrows Lijiang (the base city the group returns to) to its historic quarter Lijiang Old Town/Dayan; the walk is in the old town, but the itinerary place is the city, so the entity is a sub-area (borderline). (A and B agree.)

sources.quote: By the Song dynasty in the 10th century, Dongba was widely used by the Naxi people.
The Naxi, originally from northwestern China and having a Tibeto-Burman language with pictographic characters of their own, are mainly distributed in Lijiang

facts.rationale: UNESCO ties Dongba culture and Naxi character to the town; Dongba is the Naxi priestly tradition. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: was registered on the UNESCO World Heritage List on December 4, 1997
Date of Inscription: 1997

facts.rationale: Inscribed December 1997. (A and B agree on all fields.) Adjudicator checked Wikipedia/other quotes verbatim; UNESCO/Britannica pages return 403 to the adjudicator, quotes kept as given by both labellers.

sources.quote: entered Tibet through today's Dali Bai Autonomous Prefecture, Lijiang City and Shangri-La, and went directly to Lhasa
entered Tibet through today's Dali Bai Autonomous Prefecture, Lijiang City

facts.rationale: UNESCO and Wikipedia place Lijiang on the Tea and Horse road to Tibet. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: The streets are paved with locally quarried five-colored stone from Yulong (Jade Dragon) Snow Mountain
from where waterways feed into a network of canals and channels to supply the town

facts.rationale: Stone-paved streets (China Daily) and canals fed by snow-mountain rivers and springs (UNESCO). (A and B agree on all fields.) Adjudicator checked Wikipedia/other quotes verbatim; UNESCO/Britannica pages return 403 to the adjudicator, quotes kept as given by both labellers.

sources.quote: The Old Town of Lijiang is located on the Lijiang plain at an elevation of 2,400 meters
The Yulong Snow Mount to the north-west is the source of the rivers and springs which water the plain and supply the Heilong Pool

facts.rationale: UNESCO gives 2,400 m; Yulong (Jade Dragon) Snow Mountain lies to the north-west. (A and B agree on all fields.) Adjudicator checked Wikipedia/other quotes verbatim; UNESCO/Britannica pages return 403 to the adjudicator, quotes kept as given by both labellers.

sources.quote: is the historical center of Lijiang City, in Yunnan, China. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

facts.rationale: Old Town (Dayan) is the historic centre of Lijiang City, Yunnan; restates identity. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: is a famous pond in the scenic Jade Spring Park (Yu Quan Gong Yuan) located at the foot of Elephant Hill
from where waterways feed into a network of canals and channels to supply the town

facts.rationale: Canal network fed from Heilong (Black Dragon) Pool in Jade Spring (Yuquan) Park; timber Naxi houses per UNESCO; stone lanes per China Daily. (A and B agree on all fields.) Adjudicator checked Wikipedia/other quotes verbatim; UNESCO/Britannica pages return 403 to the adjudicator, quotes kept as given by both labellers.

sources.quote: important center for the economic and cultural communication between various ethnic groups such as the Naxi, Han, Tibetan and Bai
Numerous two-storeyed, tile-roofed, timber-framed houses combining elements of Han and Zang architecture

facts.rationale: UNESCO links the town's architecture and culture to the Naxi. (A and B agree on all fields.) Adjudicator checked Wikipedia/other quotes verbatim; UNESCO/Britannica pages return 403 to the adjudicator, quotes kept as given by both labellers.

sources.quote: The highest point is the main peak of Yulong Snow Mountain, with an elevation of 5,596 meters
Jade Dragon Snow Mountain towering over nearby Lijiang

facts.rationale: Shanzidou 5,596 m, within tolerance of 'about 5,600 m'. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: It is within the region encompassed by the Hengduan Mountains, where the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau converge.
Jade Dragon Snow Mountain towering over nearby Lijiang

facts.rationale: Lijiang lies in the Hengduan Mountains region of NW Yunnan near Jade Dragon Snow Mountain. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: the area had been hit by a devastating earthquake, which necessitated reconstruction of numerous old town structures
the area had been hit by a devastating earthquake, which necessitated reconstruction of numerous old town structures.

facts.rationale: 1996 earthquake damaged the old town, followed by reconstruction; 'much of' is slightly stronger than 'numerous structures' but consistent. (A and B agree on all fields.)
